Quarto's code annotations are a good way to explain a block line by line.
On a slide they all arrive at once, so the audience reads the last note while the speaker is still on the first.

`codefrag` makes each annotation a fragment.
The arrow keys step through them, the tooltip appears as each is revealed, and the annotations follow the highlighted lines when both are used.

## Installation

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Or install it from your editor with [Quarto Wizard](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard):

## Quick start

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    code-annotations: select
revealjs-plugins:
  - codefrag
```

Then annotate code as you would anywhere in Quarto.

`code-annotations: select` is what makes the annotations interactive; the plugin turns them into fragments from there.

## Try it

The [preview deck](preview.html) is built by this site: press the arrow keys and each annotation arrives in turn.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for the source behind the deck.

## Where it works

RevealJS.

Annotation markers are styled for print, so a PDF export keeps them legible even though the stepping is gone.
